results.title: TileWeave: Heterogeneous Tiling for Sparse Prefill on Mobile SoCs
results.abstract: Smartphone applications increasingly require large language models to process long contexts, whereas high prefill latency and memory demands constrain local inference. Block-sparse attention reduces computation and memory traffic, but its irregular selections conflict with mobile NPUs'preference for large, regular tiles. Efficient execution must exploit cross-query reuse while avoiding redundant computation and preserving selections needed for accuracy. In this paper, we present TileWeave, which partitions sparse attention by this cross-query reuse: highly shared key blocks run in coarse NPU tiles, while low-reuse blocks run on the GPU only for the query blocks that selected them. In addition, we design an NPU-native pooled-key selector that keeps selection inexpensive, and a runtime that publishes GPU partials in the order the NPU consumes them and merges them in its existing output store. On RULER, HeteroSparse matches XAttention's accuracy with Qwen3-1.7B and improves it with Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct; its mean LongBench scores match XAttention as well. On Snapdragon SM8750 and SM8850 phones, it achieves 1.35--3.23$\times$ faster full-model prefill than XAttention over 1k--16k tokens and up to 1.58$\times$ faster than dense attention.

results.title: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention
results.abstract: Long-horizon reasoning and agentic workloads strain KV-cache capacity and decode attention throughput. We present Jet-QSparse, a training-free method that combines compact NVFP4 cache storage with native FP4 query-key computation on Blackwell tensor cores. A dense scan scores the full key history and selects 128-token blocks for sparse FP16 value aggregation with FP32 accumulation, preserving higher precision in the output-forming step while enabling contiguous tile loads. Calibrated key centering and at most two BF16 pages per sequence and layer address quantization error; FP8 prefill uses a temporary arena while the persistent cache is packed directly from BF16 activations. Across four hybrid LLMs, a budget of 128 blocks per KV head shows no detected accuracy loss on the evaluated mathematical reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks, although some smaller budgets incur losses. With 64 blocks, Qwen3.8-27B achieves a $1.94\times$ end-to-end decode speedup over dense BF16 at 128K context and batch size 16 on one GB300, and the measured Qwen KV pools provide $2.58$-$2.76\times$ BF16's token capacity.
